leverage.exposure: A leveraged position is open and it outranks everything else in this briefing. The standing offer on Makengo exceeds available cash, he is the only bidder on a listing priced at market value, so the bid wins unless someone outbids it. Three outcomes exist and only two are acceptable: fund it by selling Bernardo, or withdraw the offer. Doing neither is the default if Georg does nothing, and it is a self-inflicted wipeout of the entire matchday score. Selling Bernardo back to Kickbase needs no counterparty and settles instantly, so the safe play is to do it today rather than lean on the thin gap between the auction resolving and the lock. Funding it leaves the balance positive.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is cash before the lock, not the spending floor. Because a negative balance at matchday start scores zero, the floor-based spending power is unusable this window and only settled cash counts. Once the Bernardo sale funds Makengo, what remains is too little to buy anything on the board that would improve the eleven, so the squad is effectively closed for business until MD2 has locked. There is no formation hole: the squad fills its optimal shape with a body to spare.

verdict.headline: One action decides this matchday: sell Bernardo back to Kickbase, and do it now rather than later.

verdict.detail: One action decides this matchday: sell Bernardo back to Kickbase, and do it now rather than later. The live Makengo offer resolves roughly two hours before the MD2 lock against cash that cannot cover it, and an unfunded win means a negative balance at matchday start and zero points for the whole matchday. The previous run advised waiting for the evening market-value tick before selling. That tick has now landed, and the next one falls after the lock, so the sale price is frozen for the rest of the window and there is no longer any reason to wait. Everything else this run is quiet: the board turned up nothing worth owning, the fitness sweep is clean for the second run running, and no other recommendation changed.

sell.reason: Bernardo is the sale, and the honest framing matters: this is not an availability sale. He is fit and he is a confirmed starter at left-back, verified again this run from a dated probable eleven with his positional rival absent and only one squad player doubtful. He is sold purely because he is the cleanest funding route for the Makengo offer, and the swap is a genuine upgrade rather than a wash. Kickbase's status flag on him is stale by more than three days and contradicted by every current source; it is not a reason to act and not a reason to notify. Widmer stays despite being the weakest man in the eleven, because selling him drops the squad below the shape that scores best and there is no replacement that lands in time. Lokonga stays: the standing hold makes him a keeper, and the case against him was only ever points-per-euro, never urgency.

standing.name: Bernardo

THE WAITING ARGUMENT IS NOW SPENT AND MUST NOT BE REPEATED. The previous run correctly advised waiting for the 20:00Z tick; that tick has landed (list_market mvud now reads 2026-09-04T20:00:00Z, i.e. the NEXT update is 90 minutes AFTER the MD2 lock at 18:30Z). Bernardo's mv rose 7.048.552 -> 7.156.102, exactly his tfhmvt of +107.550, so the realised gain from waiting was 107.550, not the 160.481 the old estimate projected. From here there is ZERO further upside to delaying: no tick can fall before the deadline and the sale price is frozen at 7.156.102 for the remaining ~19,3h. Any future run that repeats "wait for the tick" is wrong. Kickbase buys back at exactly mv with no counterparty, re-measured three more times this run (Blaswich 2.653.917, Tiago Tomas 9.460.597, Awortwie-Grant 1.892.782 all cleared to Kickbase at mv to the euro). After the sale cash is 11.263.624; after Makengo resolves, 2.263.624, positive. Squad dips to 11 (1GK/4DEF/4MID/2ATT, legal as 4-4-2) for the ~19h between the sale and the auction, then returns to 12 with 5-3-2 optimal. Fielded XI 1395 -> 1423, +28: ap 62 out, ap 90 in. HE IS FIT AND STARTING and this is not an availability sale - re-verified independently this run, magazin.comunio.de dated 03.09.2026 gives the Hoffenheim XI v Dortmund as Baumann - Coufal, Kabak, Hajdari, Bernardo - Wimmer, Avdullahu, Burger - Lemperle, Daghim - Hlozek, with Bernardo at LEFT-BACK, Hranac again absent, and only Prass doubtful; he is absent from the Ligainsider Verletzte-und-Gesperrte table (03.09). Kickbase still carries st 2 timestamped 2026-08-31T14:40:12Z, now ~78h stale and contradicted - do NOT notify on it. Alternatives checked and rejected this run: withdrawing the Makengo bid keeps 1395 and forfeits +28 for nothing; selling Widmer instead costs 29 fielded points and does not raise enough; Lokonga is barred as a keeper by HOLD Hj137mo.

buy.reason: Makengo is the only buy and the bid is already placed, so no new action is needed there beyond funding it. He is verified fit and in a dated probable eleven at left-back, and the daily market-value tick has quietly moved in Georg's favour, shrinking the premium the standing bid pays over market value. One caveat is worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over: a dated club report this evening frames left-back as a live contest between him and the club captain, with the coach quoted saying only that small details will decide who starts. He remains the probable starter on the balance of sources, but the rotation risk is real. Nothing else on the board survives. The single new listing since the last run is a player already on the do-not-buy list, relisted by a rival at a large markup, whose average is below every player in the current eleven. The tempting cheap Freiburg midfielder is confirmed by a second dated source to be a substitute, not a starter, and buying him would mean opening a fresh leveraged position hours before the lock to field a bench player. The one genuine upgrade on the board is a Frankfurt defender who would displace the weakest man in the eleven for a meaningful gain, but he is unaffordable this window and the only sales that could cover him are barred. He is worth revisiting once the matchday has locked and the budget is free, and a manager listing that has sat unsold for over a day invites an offer at market value rather than at the ask.
